main_text.head: ISAACI CASAVBONI AD THEOPHRASTI CHARA-CTERES ETHICOS
Liber Commentarius.
main_text.p: [?]ΔΗ μὲν καὶ πρότερον πολλάκις.] Ostendit Theophrastus, non imparatum se ad huius operis scriptionem accedere: sed re saepius secum considerata, expensaque. Ideo ait ὅτι σημαίνας τὸν διά-νοιαν[?]: familiari Aristoteli, & aliis philosophis loquendi genere. simplicius Xenophon initio Παι-δείας[?], Ἔννοια ποτὲ ἡμῖν ἐγχωρεῖ[?]. & initio Commentariorum, Πολλάκις ἐθαύμασα[?]. At noster mox quoque verbis significantissimis vtitur, σωθεωρήσας[?], & ἀπαγγελτικῶ[?]: quae dictiones, Θεάσαι inquam, & Θεωρῶν[?], à rebus diuinis originem habentes, de quibus dum attentius meditamur, fimus ipsi quodammodo diuini, & vt philosophus ait in decimo Nicomacheorum, nos ipsos ἀπαθανατίζομεν[?]: postea ad eas res sunt translatae, quas cum magna voluptate, vel magna cum attentione contemplamur. Eôdem spectat & quod ait, ὁμοιωθῆναι πανταχῶς ἀνθρώ-πων φύσειν[?]: fuit enim necesse vt qui describere ho-minum

page.notes: The large initial H (lines 2 to 4 of the paragraph) is a decorated letter; I could not match it to a joined word, so it is not reproduced as a separate word. Greek lines are small and partly smudged: all Greek is copied as best seen and marked [?] throughout, with the hyphenated Greek word split at the line end ("διά-νοιαν", "ἀνθρώ-πων"). The paragraph continues onto the next page after "ho-minum". A stray mark in the left margin and a mark at the foot of the page are not printed text and are left out.
